A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 25-page versions of the same RandLoRA paper, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish reliable correspondence of the methods, equations, results, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and commonsense-reasoning experiments, GLUE results, and rank and sparsity ablations (Figures 2–3; Tables 1–4; Appendices B and E).

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including classification, commonsense reasoning, GLUE, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same fixed random bases, learned diagonal scaling matrices, shared A matrix, and full-rank update construction. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 21/22 vision datasets, eight commonsense-reasoning tasks, GLUE tasks, and E2E training description in Appendix B.2. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including LoRA, NoLA, VeRA, full fine-tuning, and the appendix comparisons with Maple + DePT and DoRA. The corrected CoOp citation does not add an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The shot and data regimes, model configurations, parameter-matching controls, metrics, splits, and training settings in Section 5 and Appendix C are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections 6.1–6.4 and Appendix A retain identical activation-similarity, loss-landscape, update-rank, and random-basis sparsity analyses. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 still specifies five runs and reporting averages with one standard deviation for GLUE in Table 4. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported scores, plotted findings, and appendix result entries are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Llama3-8B/170k Performant accuracies of 85.2 for LoRA and 85.6 for RandLoRA.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, its assumptions, the mathematical formulations, Appendix C.6's sparsity argument, and Appendix D's lemmas, proofs, and derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim full-rank parameter-efficient adaptation and reduced performance gaps with full fine-tuning across vision, language, and vision-language tasks. The abstract edit preserves meaning; the contribution list and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of CLIP versus DinoV2 behavior, small-data overfitting, rank effects, and sparsity remain unchanged. Section 6.6 retains the same computational-overhead limitations and proposed future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical hyperparameters, implementation explanations, hardware disclosures, and training-time information. Repository and implementation links are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces CoOp's citation to Radford et al. (2021) with Zhou et al. (2022b), adding Learning to prompt for vision-language models to the bibliography. This corrects a specific attribution without changing the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract lightly rewrites the sentence about low-rank representational limitations without changing its meaning. Citation labels and caption wording receive small corrections; the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's caption changes from 'CLIP of DinoV2 vision encoder' to 'CLIP and DinoV2 vision encoders.' Its plots, axes, and legends remain identical, as do all other figures and tables; abstract and bibliography edits cause only local text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves attribution by replacing CoOp's CLIP-paper citation with the dedicated prompt-learning reference, and clarifies Figure 2's caption. These are limited improvements in scholarly accuracy and clarity; the scientific content, evidence, and appendices remain unchanged.
